subsection: H. Directors and Officers Liability (D&O) Insurance
text: [Winkler v. National Union Fire Ins. Co. of Pittsburgh (9th Cir. 1991) 930 F2d 1364, 1366 (applying Calif. law)] • [3:679] On the other hand, a letter demanding monetary compensation for alleged employment discrimination and threatening suit was a “claim” even though the letter did not mention a specific dollar amount: “[T]he insistence on compensation by way of settlement in lieu of litigation constituted a demand for ‘civil damages or other relief’ within the ordinary meaning of those words.” [Westrec Marina Mgmt., Inc. v. Arrowood Indem. Co. (2008) 163 CA4th 1387, 1393, 78 CR3d 264, 269—delay in reporting claim excused insurer's duty to indemnify or defend suit] [3:680 - 3:689] Reserved. 4. [3:690] Relevant Exclusions: A D&O policy may specifically exclude employment-related claims. In the absence of such an exclusion, several exclusions typically found in D&O policies may be relevant to such claims: a. [3:691] “Insured vs. insured” exclusion: D&O policies typically exclude coverage for actions brought by one insured director or officer against another (usually excepting shareholder derivative suits).
